fields.Frequency: Seasonal (annual pre-positioning June); event-driven per typhoon
fields.Participants: VP Supply Chain, Merchandising, DC Ops, Logistics, Store Ops
fields.Trigger: PAGASA typhoon season advisory (June–November) or approaching tropical cyclone
fields.Volume: 1 annual plan; 8–12 event-driven activations per year

workflows.name: Typhoon Season Pre-Positioning & Emergency Stock Planning

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "reviews prior year demand curves by region" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-calculate of "calculates pre-position quantities per DC region based on historical typhoon…" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "Logistics pre-books surge delivery capacity with 3PL partners" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: maintaining flexible inter-DC transfer capability
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stockout risk**: If typhoon shifts track after pre-positioning, stock is stranded in wrong DC; mitigated by maintaining flexible inter-DC transfer capability
- **Overstock risk**: Mild typhoon season leads to excess emergency inventory requiring markdown; mitigated by CTL-232 (typhoon-response protocol execution)
System Touchpoints: - Demand planning module for surge forecasting (historical typhoon demand patterns)
- Inventory reservation for emergency stock segregation
- PO generation for emergency procurement
Time Estimate: - 30–120 min per occurrence; annual planning phase ~5–7 business days

steps.activity: Merchandising identifies emergency merchandise categories: tarps, plywood, nails, waterproofing, flashlights, batteries, water containers, generators, ropes, sandbags; reviews prior year demand curves by region

Supply Chain calculates pre-position quantities per DC region based on historical typhoon impact zones; coordinates emergency POs with vendors; arranges early shipments to high-risk DCs (Visayas, Bicol)
DC Ops allocates dedicated emergency staging areas; ensures stock is segregated and tagged as emergency reserve; Logistics pre-books surge delivery capacity with 3PL partners

fields.Frequency: 8–15 activations per store per year (regional variance)
fields.Participants: Store Manager, All Store Staff, Regional Manager
fields.Trigger: PAGASA Signal No. 1 raised in store region or typhoon within 48-hour projected path
fields.Volume: Up to 200 stores simultaneously for nationwide typhoons

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "Store Manager receives automated PAGASA alert via ERP dashboard" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-test of "test backup generator, verify fuel levels, charge POS terminals for offline…" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "reviews status across affected region" (replaces manual Step 3).
Pain Points / Risks: - **Staffing gaps**: Typhoon approaching during shift change or non-operating hours delays execution
- **Communication failure**: Power/internet loss before checklist completion; mitigated by SMS backup alerts
System Touchpoints: - Mobile store operations app for checklist execution and status reporting
- POS offline mode readiness verification

- **Custody & precedence** (per the [Event Custody & Precedence Register](../event-custody-and-precedence-register.md), E-01): the Signal 1 store readiness checklist is the canon; BCP protocol activation/monitoring runs VS-26 W848 with VS-26 W1221's regional supervision layer over it; HSE preparedness activation per VS-24 W1386 (Signal 3, or Signal 2 with forecast intensification); the closure decision (Signal 3+/LGU order) always follows W2510

steps.activity: Store Manager receives automated PAGASA alert via ERP dashboard; initiates typhoon readiness checklist: secure outdoor lumber yard, move chemicals to elevated shelving, cover tile displays, sandbag entrances
Staff executes facility checklist: test backup generator, verify fuel levels, charge POS terminals for offline mode, secure cash in safe, backup local POS data
Store Manager confirms checklist completion via mobile app; Regional Manager reviews status across affected region; escalates incomplete stores

fields.Participants: DC Ops Manager, Warehouse Supervisors, Logistics, Safety Officer
fields.Trigger: PAGASA Signal No. 2 in DC region or typhoon within 36-hour projected path
fields.Volume: 4 DCs; up to all 4 simultaneously for super typhoons

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "verify fire suppression systems" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "Logistics Manager cancels or reroutes scheduled 3PL deliveries" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-436 (ensure controlled execution — Typhoon Preparedness & Early Warning Operations (PA-69.1).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Inventory damage**: Flooding at DC3 (Calamba, Laguna — flood-prone) or DC2 (Cebu port area) during severe typhoons
- **Supply chain disruption**: Multi-day DC closure affects replenishment to 50–60 stores
System Touchpoints: - WMS for inventory relocation tracking and hazmat segregation
- TMS for shipment rerouting and cancellation
- Fleet GPS for vehicle positioning

- **Custody & precedence** (per the [Event Custody & Precedence Register](../event-custody-and-precedence-register.md), E-01/E-04): DC-level preparedness is this workflow's canon (stores run the W2503 checklist); DC power contingency and typhoon fuel logistics chain to W2514; BCP protocol context per VS-26 W848

steps.activity: DC Ops Manager activates typhoon protocol: halt outbound shipments to affected stores, expedite any in-transit deliveries, secure dock doors, move ground-level inventory to upper racks or elevated areas
Warehouse Supervisors secure hazardous materials (paint, solvents, chemicals) per DENR hazmat protocols; verify fire suppression systems; test emergency lighting and backup power
Logistics Manager cancels or reroutes scheduled 3PL deliveries; secures fleet vehicles in covered areas or higher ground; activates driver safety stand-down

fields.Participants: Merch Planner, Supply Planning, Procurement, Finance
fields.Trigger: PAGASA Signal No. 2+ or post-disaster assessment indicating severe impact area

Automation Opportunity: - System rule-based auto-approval of "approves emergency procurement budget" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-update of "updates emergency stock allocation rules" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-436 (ensure controlled execution — Typhoon Preparedness & Early Warning Operations (PA-69.1).)
- operational: Merchandise Planner review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Forecast accuracy**: Each typhoon is unique; overreliance on historical averages may miss category shifts
- **Vendor capacity**: All retailers compete for same emergency supplies simultaneously
System Touchpoints: - Demand planning module with typhoon scenario modeling
- Automated PO generation with emergency approval workflow
- Inventory allocation engine with disaster priority rules
Time Estimate: - 2–4 hours per occurrence for model updates; 1–2 days for full planning cycle

steps.activity: Planner models demand surge using historical typhoon data by region and severity: tarps (+400%), plywood (+300%), nails (+250%), waterproofing (+500%), generators (+200%); adjusts by Signal level and population density

Supply Planning converts forecast to emergency PO recommendations; Procurement contacts vendors for expedited shipments; Finance pre-approves emergency procurement budget (PHP 50M–200M per major typhoon)
System updates emergency stock allocation rules: prioritizes hardest-hit stores, overrides normal ABC allocation, enables automatic replenishment triggers at reduced ROP thresholds

fields.Participants: Marketing Comm Mgr, Store Ops, Customer Service
fields.Trigger: PAGASA Signal No. 1 in store region
fields.Volume: SMS/push to ~600,000 loyalty members; regional targeting

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "Marketing drafts typhoon preparedness advisory" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "accounts with project-specific material securing advice" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-post of "Customer Service prepares FAQ responses" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-436 (ensure controlled execution — Typhoon Preparedness & Early Warning Operations (PA-69.1).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Message fatigue**: Over-alerting for minor storms reduces customer responsiveness for severe events
- **Misinformation**: Premature operating hour changes create confusion if typhoon track shifts
System Touchpoints: - CRM/loyalty platform for segmented communication
- Omnichannel notification system
- Ecommerce banner management for typhoon advisories

steps.activity: Marketing drafts typhoon preparedness advisory: product recommendations (tarps, waterproofing, emergency supplies), store operating hour updates, BOPIS availability, safety tips; targets by affected region

System sends segmented communications: SMS to loyalty members in affected region, push notifications via app, social media posts, email to trade/corporate accounts with project-specific material securing advice
Customer Service prepares FAQ responses: store hours, product availability, return policy extensions for typhoon-affected areas, delivery postponement procedures

fields.Participants: Pricing Mgr, Legal, Merchandising, Store Ops
fields.Trigger: PAGASA Signal No. 2+ or DTI price monitoring alert in affected region

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "documents compliance for DTI audit trail" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **DTI penalties**: Price freeze violations carry fines of PHP 5,000–1,000,000 per violation under RA 7581
- **Margin erosion**: Extended price freezes during supply cost increases reduce profitability
System Touchpoints: - Pricing engine with emergency freeze toggle per region/category
- POS price enforcement with override blocking
- DTI compliance reporting and audit log

steps.activity: Pricing Manager activates emergency pricing freeze for disaster-essential items (construction materials, basic hardware, emergency supplies) per DTI price control regulations (RA 7581 — Price Act); locks SRP in system for affected region
Legal confirms DTI compliance: no price increases above SRP during declared disaster period; system blocks all promotional markdown overrides and manual price changes for frozen categories
Store Ops verifies POS price sync across affected stores; confirms price labels on shelf; documents compliance for DTI audit trail

fields.Participants: Treasury Analyst, Store Manager, CIT Service, Finance
fields.Trigger: PAGASA Signal No. 1 in store region

workflows.name: Pre-Typhoon Cash Float & Payment Contingency Setup

Automation Opportunity: - System workflow orchestration of "coordinates expedited CIT delivery" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-generate of "imprint capability, confirms change fund adequacy" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-schedule of "Finance monitors bank branch closures in affected areas" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cash security**: Increased float during civil disturbance risk period
- **Banking disruption**: Multi-day bank closures in severely affected areas delay deposits
System Touchpoints: - Treasury cash position module with disaster override
- POS offline payment cache management
- CIT scheduling integration with emergency priority

steps.activity: Treasury increases cash float for affected stores by 50% to handle surge in cash transactions (GCash/e-wallet outages common during typhoons); coordinates expedited CIT delivery
Store Manager activates payment contingency: verifies offline POS payment cache, tests manual credit card imprint capability, confirms change fund adequacy
Finance monitors bank branch closures in affected areas; adjusts cash deposit schedules; authorizes extended cash holding at stores with bank holiday overrides

fields.Participants: HR Ops Mgr, Store Managers, DC Ops Managers, Safety Officer
fields.Trigger: PAGASA Signal No. 1 in store/DC region or management decision

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-track of "HR activates emergency notification system" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-post of "post-typhoon reopening, arrange overnight shelter for essential staff at…" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinates emergency salary advances or relief assistance per company policy" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-436 (ensure controlled execution — Typhoon Preparedness & Early Warning Operations (PA-69.1).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Communication blackout**: SMS/phone networks overwhelmed during peak typhoon; mitigated by backup radio communication
- **Employee displacement**: Staff unable to report for days due to flooding or damaged housing
System Touchpoints: - HR emergency notification system with two-way messaging
- Employee self-service portal for safety check-in
- Payroll emergency advance processing module
Time Estimate: - 2–4 hours per activation; post-event tracking 24–72 hours

steps.activity: HR activates emergency notification system: SMS blast to all employees in affected region with safety instructions, reporting requirements, emergency contacts; confirms employee location and safety via response tracking

Store/DC Managers implement staffing contingency: pre-identify skeleton crew for immediate post-typhoon reopening, arrange overnight shelter for essential staff at store/DC if needed, cancel employee travel to affected areas
HR tracks employee safety status post-typhoon; activates employee assistance program for affected staff; coordinates emergency salary advances or relief assistance per company policy
